solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Correctly believe ceremony's on the radio

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is only heard, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: to buy a story is to believe it; rites are ceremonies

explanation.surface: A broadcaster insists a ceremony is being described properly on air.
explanation.walkthrough: BUY (believe, as in 'I don't buy that') plus RITES (ceremony's) said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: By rights is an idiom meaning properly or justly, which is what correctly conveys.

clue.text: Initially, Bible-basher was manager of church's regional office

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: its first letter is B
to have run a business is to have managed it
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An evangelical preacher once ran a church's local office.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a local division of a company or organisation, an outpost of the head office.

clue.text: Leader in synagogue and Buddhist finally talk at length

parts.note: a rabbi leads a Jewish congregation

indicators.note: finally takes just the closing letter of Buddhist

parts.note: its last letter is T

explanation.surface: Religious leaders of two faiths hold a long conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader in' looks like a first-letter signal, but the whole phrase is the religious leader. To rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit on is to chatter endlessly, so rabbit means to talk without stopping.

clue.text: Loose blouse I put among clothes laid out

indicators.note: put among places the letter I inside the word for clothes

parts.note: garb is clothing

indicators.note: laid out suggests letters spread and rearranged into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder giving ALDI

explanation.surface: Someone places a blouse among clothes spread out on the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: GARB with I put among it makes GARIB; LAID rearranged by 'out' gives ALDI.
explanation.definitionFit: A garibaldi is a loose women's blouse modelled on the red shirts of Garibaldi's soldiers.

clue.text: Brass tacks article on one of Capone's men, reportedly uncompromising

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the gangster's name is taken by sound

parts.note: Frank Nitti was a henchman of Al Capone
gritty means tough and uncompromising

explanation.surface: A news article about a tough gangster in Capone's mob.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Nitti, Al Capone's enforcer, sounds like NITTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to brass tacks means dealing with the basic facts, the same idiom as the nitty-gritty.

clue.text: Action taken by us to protect large marine mammal

indicators.note: taken by places the word for action before us
to protect is to surround, so the outer letters wrap around the letter for large

parts.note: war is military action
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
taken as written

explanation.surface: We take steps to defend a big sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' means the war-and-us pair wraps around the letter for large rather than the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: The walrus is a large tusked sea mammal of Arctic waters, related to seals.

clue.text: Tree in a small enclosure

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: A tree growing inside a little fenced plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar with trembling leaves, a common woodland species.

clue.text: Modest, bowing out

definitions.meaning: second meaning: leaving a job or competition for good

explanation.walkthrough: The two phrases are separate meanings of one word: an adjective for shyness and a participle for stepping down.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring person is shy and reserved, and someone retiring is giving up work or withdrawing.

clue.text: Bring over short gypsy girl's telescope

indicators.note: to bring something over is to turn it, so the shortened word is read backwards
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: loses its final Y to give GYPS
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a gypsy girl's telescope to be handed across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring over' reads like handing something across, but it turns the shortened word back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small hand-held telescope, the kind associated with sailors.

clue.text: Officer material, star batman heading off abroad

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing woollen fabric

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered all over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter

parts.note: without its first letter B gives ATMAN

explanation.surface: A soldier's servant, a batman, travelling overseas in fine material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' strips BATMAN to ATMAN; STAR plus ATMAN, rearranged by 'abroad', gives ANTATARMS. A batman is an officer's servant in the British army.
explanation.definitionFit: A serjeant-at-arms is an official who keeps order in a parliament or court, an officer of the house.

clue.text: Vegetable that's given away in French inn

indicators.note: something given away is lost, so these letters are dropped from the vegetable

parts.note: an aubergine is an eggplant

explanation.surface: An eggplant handed out free at a country inn in France.
explanation.walkthrough: AUBERGINE is the British word for eggplant; removing IN leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An auberge is a country inn or hostelry in France, offering lodging and meals.

clue.text: Compassion of European politician at hospital close to bankruptcy

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
H is the map-sign abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: close to means the end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: its last letter is Y

explanation.surface: A Euro MP visits a hospital nearly bankrupt and shows sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is the capacity to share and understand another's feelings, closely akin to sympathy.

clue.text: Cold, member making ascent

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: Mountaineers in freezing weather, one member of the party making the ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' reads as a club member, but here it is an arm or leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb, as a noun, is a going upward, the act of mounting a slope or rising.

clue.text: Mostly at home with army officer

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A retired army officer who usually stays home.
explanation.definitionFit: In general is an idiom meaning usually or on the whole, for the most part.

clue.text: Cash lost in 'em in resort?

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it means sort again, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder of twelve letters

explanation.surface: Gamblers at a seaside resort lose their money in the arcade machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town, which is also the setting for the whole clue; read as re-sort it rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamblers feed coins into these one-armed bandits at seaside towns and casinos and mostly lose their money.

clue.text: Brutus, for one, in musical number

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a number is a piece of music

explanation.surface: Brutus, Caesar's assassin, appearing in a song from a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Brutus looks like Caesar's assassin; here it is an eighteenth-century style of wig, so a hairpiece is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A brutus was a rough cropped wig worn in the eighteenth century, an example of a false head covering.

clue.text: Beggar born on barge

indicators.note: on places the first piece above the second in this down answer

parts.note: B is the genealogical abbreviation for born
a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for loading ships

explanation.surface: A poor beggar born aboard a canal barge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beggar' looks like a person asking for money, but here it is a mild insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighter and beggar are both mild British insults for a rascal or unlucky fellow.

clue.text: Evasive about being put in charge

indicators.note: being put in places the word for about inside the word for charge

parts.note: to indict is to formally charge with a crime
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A suspect dodges questions about being placed in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in charge' looks like a phrase meaning promoted, but the clue splits it: 'put in' is the insertion and 'charge' is INDICT.
explanation.definitionFit: An indirect answer avoids the point, much as an evasive one dodges it.

clue.text: After touching down, take off from here?

definitions.text: After touching down, take off from here?

parts.note: an aircraft is landing when it touches down
to strip is to take off clothes

explanation.surface: A plane lands and then departs again from the same airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works as a description of a runway too: planes land there and take off from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing strip is a basic runway where aircraft land and depart.

clue.text: Altogether popular, Miss Gale's best friend?

parts.note: something in is fashionable and popular
Dorothy Gale's dog in The Wizard of Oz is Toto

explanation.surface: A popular dog, best friend of Dorothy in The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for as a whole or entirely, the same sense as completely.

clue.text: Played Sawgrass, say, with shot with iron across lake ending in hazard

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the pair of words straddle the letter for lake

parts.note: a go is a shot or attempt
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: ending in takes the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its last letter is D

explanation.surface: A golfer at Sawgrass hits an iron over the lake into a hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: Sawgrass (TPC Sawgrass in Florida) is a famous golf course, with an island green over water. GO and FE straddle L to make GOLFE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have played a round at a famous course is to have golfed, Sawgrass being an example.

clue.text: Musician's good universal appeal playing sitar

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
it means sex appeal

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with and put in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder giving ARIST

explanation.surface: A talented musician whose playing of the sitar is widely loved.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for appeal comes from the old phrase for sex appeal. SITAR rearranged by 'playing' gives ARIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitarist is a player of the guitar, one kind of instrumentalist.

clue.text: Prevent a check pinning rook

indicators.note: pinning holds the letter for rook inside the word for check

parts.note: to vet is to check
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess move: check while pinning the opponent's rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' and 'pinning' look like chess terms, but check is VET and pinning holds R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a disaster is to stop it from happening, warding it off in advance.

clue.text: Quietly enthusiastic about piebald horse

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: A rider is quietly keen on a patched horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a horse with patches of white and another colour, the American term for a skewbald or piebald.

clue.text: Danger involving English on that account

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the threat holds the letter for English

parts.note: a threat is a danger

explanation.surface: A danger involving the English, and the reason for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereat is an archaic adverb meaning for that reason, or at that place.

clue.text: Quickly list items in roll of film no longer available

parts.note: a reel is a roll of film
a dish that is off the menu is no longer available

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper rattles off what is in a film roll that is sold out.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel off a list is to recite it rapidly and fluently without pause.

clue.text: Go round old gallery, following king

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the king comes first and the rest follows

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A visitor tours an old gallery, trailing behind the king.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is London's famous art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn about an axis, spinning in a circle.

clue.text: Heavenly body of a bodybuilder?

parts.note: a steroid is a drug that builds muscle, so it is a body builder

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder with a divine physique, a heavenly body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' looks like praise of a physique; it is the definition, a rock in space. A steroid builds the body.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a minor planet orbiting the sun, an example of an object in space.
